name: Kildin Sami

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Kildin Saami (kild1236).

notes: Research. Kildin Sami is a Kola (Eastern) Saami language of the Uralic family, written in an extended Cyrillic alphabet (Kert 1971 orthography, revised 1980s). The map covers the base Cyrillic letters plus the language-specific graphemes: Ӈ (velar nasal), the voiceless-sonorant letters Ӆ Ӎ Ӊ Ҏ, the voiceless glide Ҋ, and Һ (marking preaspiration). Iotated Е Ё Ю Я are given their glide+vowel reading. Vowel length is written with a combining macron over the base vowel letter (а̄ э̄ ы̄ о̄ я̄ ю̄ е̄) or, for и/у, with the dedicated precomposed letters Ӣ/Ӯ; both are modelled as long vowels here (Kert 1971), which is the largest single source of the pre-upgrade PER gap. Word stress is fixed on the first syllable (Kert 1971). Suprasegmental palatalization signalled by Ь/Ҍ/Ъ is mostly orthographically silent in the sampled gold (it marks a preceding consonant's place/manner distinction lexically rather than adding a segment) and is left unencoded as a known engine-limit gap; the one exception observed (⟨хь⟩ realising as a single palatalised [çː]) is a closed pattern too small to justify a general rule from this sample and is not yet modelled.
